requirement:
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
rationale:
## Judgment

The sources and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. No unacknowledged gap was found.

## Obligations and coverage

1. **Construct each mandatory set by combining the applicable contributions.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#impl[AuthoringSubject]/fn[sources]` dispatches to `prepare`, `prepare_citation`, or `prepare_site` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`. Those methods assemble the subject, applicable declarations, source nodes, built-in text, and terminology dependencies. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[reference_selector]` selects the contributing declaration, owning outline node, or plain-text file. Coverage includes `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]`, `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs]`, and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]`. Citation and site assembly are also asserted by `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_review_inputs_combine_item_declarations_terms_and_built_ins_once]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]`.

2. **A contributing requirement must cite this requirement.** The contribution declarations in `requirements.authoring_input`, `requirements.examples.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.ci.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.references.citation_review`, and `requirements.references.site_review` cite `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.

3. **A contributing requirement must define its contributed sources.** Those declarations identify respectively the subject declaration, reference targets and anchors, terminology declarations, exclusion of earlier evidence, citation-review inputs, and site-review inputs.

4. **A contributing requirement must define when its contribution applies.** The same declarations specify requirement authoring, example authoring, direct outgoing reference edges, terminology dependencies of contributed inputs, reassessment with earlier evidence, citation reviews, or site reviews. These textual obligations need no runtime test.

5. **Include every applicable contribution.** The three preparation methods combine those contributions; `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[definition_inputs]` obtains transitive terminology dependencies through `src/terms.rs#fn[dependencies]`. The assembly tests above assert the resulting sets. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` additionally verifies anchored contributions, and `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[earlier_evidence_inputs_and_judgments_are_not_carried_forward]` verifies the existing-evidence exclusion.

6. **Deduplicate identical selections.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[insert_selector]` checks selector membership before insertion. Preparation also deduplicates terminology inputs and built-in names. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` verifies that identical implementation and test anchors produce one input; `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_review_inputs_combine_item_declarations_terms_and_built_ins_once]` explicitly asserts one input per repeated declaration, shared term, and built-in.

7. **Report unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[source_input]` checks source access and propagates selection-resolution failures. Anchor resolution in `prepare` adds the subject and anchor to the error. `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[configured_record]` prepares sources before connecting to the model provider. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference]` checks missing files, missing nodes, and denied anchors. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[unresolvable_mandatory_inputs_fail_before_any_model_request]` verifies failure reporting and that the model endpoint is not contacted.

8. **Supply the complete set in the initial model request.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[initial_prompt]` serializes `model_mandatory_inputs`; `assess` passes that prompt to `converse`, which sends it to the provider. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` checks the initial request for the requirement, implementation, test, terminology, and FIXME material. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_the_item_and_citations]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` cover the separate citation and site prompt paths.

9. **Omit project-root generated evidence by default, including symlink aliases.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[generated_evidence_path]` checks lexical and canonical paths. `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[omit_generated_evidence]` applies the omission decision in preparation. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_anchors_are_omitted_unless_allowed_and_abort_when_disallowed]` verifies default omission for both direct paths and symlink aliases. `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_evidence_references_are_omitted_by_default]` covers reference contributions.

10. **Explicit workspace allow must permit those selections.** `omit_generated_evidence` does not omit explicitly allowed paths, and `src/authoring/access.rs#impl[SourceAccess]/fn[path]` accepts them after checking disallow. The generated-evidence anchor test above asserts that an explicitly allowed report becomes mandatory.

11. **Explicit disallow must abort under `requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.** `omit_generated_evidence` deliberately leaves explicitly disallowed selections for the access check; `SourceAccess::path` returns the denial, which preparation propagates before provider connection. The generated-evidence anchor test asserts `PermissionDenied` and the report path. The CLI failure test independently verifies the pre-request abort. This assesses the subject's application of the cited denial requirement, not that requirement's separate batch and usage obligations.

All implementation locations used for these conclusions are marked roots or reachable helpers, and the tests identified above carry references to the subject.

text: :::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} read_denial.mandatory
When source-access policy denies a mandatory input, the assessment MUST abort
before any model request and report the denied path and reason to its caller;
for an untracked file, the report MUST say what {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.untracked`
says. The aborted assessment MUST NOT write evidence or emit evidence JSON, and
its usage record MUST identify the failure. In a batch, other assessments MUST
continue, including queued assessments, and their successful writes MUST be
retained; the command MUST return a nonzero exit status after the batch
finishes.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When `habeas author` assesses a subject with existing evidence, that evidence
MUST only determine whether the subject needs assessment. Its inputs,
determination, and rationale MUST NOT contribute to the mandatory input set
defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` or otherwise be
supplied to the model. A new assessment's evidence MUST record only the inputs
supplied to it, so sources that an earlier assessment read but that no longer
exist or are no longer relevant cannot block or shape reassessment.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.

An in-source `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference to the subject, except a `{fixme}` inside one of the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, contributes the source containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
:::{req} authoring_input
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its fenced declaration, including its complete body but excluding anchor option lines, MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation. Validation MUST
remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
